author: A friend you have not met

#A Note on Ethics

This book teaches the art of opening locks. Whether you use that art to rescue a trapped friend or to relieve a merchant of his silver is your affair. I will only say that the guards of every hold have long memories and short tempers.

#The Feel of the Lock

A lock is a small machine that wants to stay closed. Your pick is a polite request that it reconsider. You must listen to it, not with your ears but with your fingertips.

Turn the pick slowly. When you feel the slightest give, the faintest shift, you have found the sweet spot. Turn the lock then, gently. Force breaks picks. Patience opens doors.

#Picks Will Break

Every lockpicker breaks picks. The difference between a novice and a master is that the master breaks fewer, and is not surprised when one snaps. Carry more than you think you will need. Then carry a few more.

#Harder Locks

The better the lock, the smaller the sweet spot. An apprentice-level lock on a farmer's chest forgives clumsy hands. A master lock on a jarl's strongbox forgives nothing.

Practice on easy locks until your fingers know the motion without thinking. Only then try your luck on the hard ones.

#One Last Thing

If you hear footsteps while you are working on a lock, stop. Stand up. Look bored. A person examining a door is merely curious. A person kneeling at a door with a bent wire in their hand is something else entirely.
